public_rationale: The broad denial of labor automation is contradicted on the stated task-level reading. In May 2025, CX Dive reported that Klarna's deployed assistant still handled two-thirds of customer inquiries, based on its spokesperson's account. That is substantial task automation, although it does not establish complete job replacement, satisfactory resolution of every inquiry, or net financial returns. The same report describes quality concerns and renewed human recruitment. METR also found slower work in one coding setting. These limits matter, but do not establish that generative AI cannot automate labor. The marketing and industry-wide returns clauses remain unproven either way.
limitations: The decisive deployment figure is company-reported through a news outlet, not independently measured.
The result depends on reading the sentence as denying substantial task automation. A narrower claim about industry-wide profitability would remain unresolved.
The assessment does not establish that generative AI generally delivers its marketing promises.
Quality problems and the continuing need for human service limit what the automation figure demonstrates.

our_interpretation: Read as a present-tense claim about deployed generative AI capabilities, rather than a forecast.
With no reporting period specified, use April–June 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication.

The plain reading denies meaningful business returns and labor automation. A documented deployment performing a substantial share of work previously requiring people can contradict the automation clause.
Task automation does not require eliminating whole jobs. Handling inquiries does not establish that every inquiry was resolved satisfactorily.
Business returns require benefits exceeding relevant costs. Usage, productivity, revenue growth and gross savings alone do not establish net returns.
The marketing clause requires matching an identifiable advertised capability to evidence about its delivery. The cloud-platform comparison supplies no separate measurable threshold.
The claim concerns general capabilities, not a named company's financial metric; metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Representative deployment evidence shows that advertised capabilities were not delivered and that actual capabilities produced neither positive business returns nor substantial automation of human tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence within the target period documents substantial task automation or positive realized business returns from deployed generative AI. This contradicts the broad denial without establishing that all marketing promises were fulfilled.
